title: SLE nucleic-acid / interferon / B-cell circuit — scientific candidate
releaseNote: Provisional editorial appraisal of sle-curated-candidate-001. Agent-authored preliminary appraisal of the frozen selected reports, not a systematic review. Abstract-only access limits critical quality assessment; independent study groups and dataset families have not been established. Weight concerns this bounded mechanism context, not clinical effectiveness or disease-wide importance. Context-mismatched treatment claims are excluded from mechanistic ratings. No calibration or independent reviewer decision is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

claims.text: Reduced engulfment in SLE-derived macrophage cultures could leave apoptotic material available.
limitations: Persistence in vivo is a proposed consequence, not directly measured by this assay.

claims.text: Persistent apoptotic material was proposed as antigen for immune-complex formation.
limitations: The paper discusses this route; it does not experimentally establish the complete downstream circuit.

claims.text: RNA-containing self-antigen is a component of the stimulatory immune complexes.
limitations: A component relationship; antigen alone does not establish a pathogenic complex.

claims.text: DNA-containing self-antigen is a component of the stimulatory immune complexes.
limitations: A component relationship; not every self-DNA molecule is immunostimulatory.

claims.text: Self-reactive antibodies participate in nucleic-acid-containing immune complexes.
limitations: Complex composition and delivery determine activity.

claims.text: RNA-containing immune complexes stimulate the TLR7-dependent culture response.
limitations: Inhibitor-based culture experiments; not evidence that all SLE is TLR7-dependent.

claims.text: DNA-containing immune complexes stimulate the TLR9-dependent culture response.
limitations: Does not establish that TLR9 has only disease-promoting effects in vivo.

claims.text: TLR7 sensing contributes to activation of pDC interferon production in the assay.
limitations: The node compresses intracellular steps; the arrow is not a direct cell-to-cell interaction.

claims.text: TLR9 sensing contributes to activation of pDC interferon production in the assay.
limitations: Culture context; this branch is not interchangeable with TLR7 in every disease model.

claims.text: Stimulated pDCs release IFN-α in the nucleic-acid immune-complex cultures.
limitations: pDCs are not asserted to be the sole interferon source in SLE.

claims.text: Type I interferons signal through the IFNAR receptor complex, which includes IFNAR1.
limitations: The label supplies receptor pharmacology, not a causal SLE experiment.

claims.text: IFN-α increased BLyS surface mobilization and release in human monocyte cultures.
limitations: Magnitude depended on cell source and disease activity; not proof of a complete in vivo loop.

claims.text: IFN-α-treated SLE monocytes mobilized intracellular BLyS to the surface and released it.
limitations: Cultured monocytes; release differs from transcription and systemic circulating concentration.

claims.text: SLE immune complexes increased surface BLyS in healthy monocyte cultures.
limitations: Indirect route through monocytes; not direct IC–BAFF binding.

claims.text: BAFF overexpression expanded mature B-cell populations in transgenic mice.
limitations: A gain-of-expression mouse model; human autoreactive-cell survival also has regulatory-label support.

claims.text: The rare TLR7 Y264H variant increased ligand sensing and caused lupus in the engineered model.
limitations: Rare human case plus mouse experiments; not a prevalence estimate or general cause of SLE.

claims.text: Enhanced TLR7 signaling increased survival of BCR-activated B cells in Y264H mice.
limitations: Functional phenotype is from engineered mice, not a direct survival measurement across human SLE.

claims.text: Type I IFN promoted plasmablast differentiation of CD40-activated human B cells.
limitations: Virus-stimulated culture system; B-cell activation is a prerequisite, and SLE transfer is a hypothesis.

claims.text: Type I IFN generated non-Ig-secreting plasmablasts in the B-cell culture system.
limitations: Does not imply IFN alone creates autoreactive plasma cells.

claims.text: Virus-stimulated pDC cultures supplied IL-6 during B-cell differentiation.
limitations: Viral stimulus, not a lupus-specific induction experiment.

claims.text: IL-6 enabled Ig-secreting plasma-cell differentiation after the type I IFN step.
limitations: Sequential and activation-dependent culture mechanism.

claims.text: The IFN-generated plasmablasts matured into Ig-secreting cells with IL-6.
limitations: Culture-defined stages; does not establish long-lived plasma-cell maintenance in SLE.

claims.text: Expanded ASC clones contributed serum autoantibodies during acute human SLE.
limitations: Observational clonal analysis; not every ASC clone is autoreactive.

claims.text: Deposited immune complexes engage an Fc-receptor-dependent inflammatory pathway in the renal mouse model.
limitations: Pathway inferred from γ-chain deletion; renal complexes are not shown to match the pDC assay complexes.

claims.text: Fc-receptor γ-chain deficiency protected lupus-prone mice from severe nephritis.
limitations: Mouse knockout evidence; does not identify a single human receptor or justify human inhibition.

claims.text: Renal immune-complex deposition is upstream of the inflammatory pathway investigated in lupus-prone mice.
limitations: Deposition alone is insufficient for severe nephritis in this model.

claims.text: Mice lacking the Fc-receptor γ chain deposited complexes and activated complement without severe nephritis.
limitations: Qualifies any claim that deposition alone is sufficient.

claims.text: SLE sera with interferon-inducing activity were especially found in active disease.
limitations: Cross-sectional correlation and healthy-donor culture response do not establish causal direction.

claims.text: Binds soluble BLyS and limits its receptor engagement on B cells.
limitations: Severe active CNS lupus was not evaluated; infection, hypersensitivity and SJS/TEN risks. Approval does not establish benefit for every phenotype.

claims.text: Active SLE or active lupus nephritis in patients aged 5 years and older receiving standard therapy. US licensed indication.
limitations: Jurisdiction and indication are specific to the cited source.

claims.text: BLISS-52 reported a higher week-52 SRI response with belimumab plus standard care than placebo plus standard care.
limitations: Trial-specific endpoint and background care; not universal response or a direct measure of mechanistic weight.

claims.text: Binds IFNAR1 and inhibits type I interferon signaling.
limitations: Severe active lupus nephritis and severe active CNS lupus were not evaluated; infection and herpes-zoster risks.

claims.text: Adults with moderate-to-severe SLE receiving standard therapy. US licensed indication.
limitations: Jurisdiction and indication are specific to the cited source.

claims.text: TULIP-2 met its BICLA response endpoint with anifrolumab plus standard therapy.
limitations: Trial-specific endpoint and background care; not universal response or a direct measure of mechanistic weight.

claims.text: TULIP-1 did not meet its SRI-4 primary endpoint; efficacy depends on the outcome definition.
limitations: Negative primary endpoint limits efficacy interpretation; it does not negate target binding.

claims.text: Inhibits TLR7/8 signaling; TLR8 is outside this bounded map.
limitations: WILLOW Cohort B missed the primary dose-response objective. Skin-trial development is not proof of broad systemic efficacy.

claims.text: Phase 3 ELOWEN program studies active cutaneous lupus manifestations with or without systemic disease. Investigational phase 3 program; no approval asserted.
limitations: Sponsor status report is not evidence of efficacy or regulatory approval.

claims.text: WILLOW Cohort B reported numerically higher BICLA responses in the enpatoran groups.
limitations: Trial-specific endpoint and background care; not universal response or a direct measure of mechanistic weight.

claims.text: WILLOW Cohort B failed its primary statistically significant dose-dependent BICLA objective.
limitations: Negative primary endpoint limits efficacy interpretation; it does not negate target binding.

claims.text: TLR9-deficient lupus-prone mice had increased pDC activation and IFN-α, qualifying a uniformly disease-promoting interpretation of TLR9 sensing.
limitations: Does not contradict the culture sensing result; deletion experiments reveal a different net regulatory role in a mouse disease model.
